newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish PZU to pay PLN 160 mln in flood damages.
newsitem.headline: Polish PZU to pay PLN 160 mln in flood damages.

text.p: Poland's largest insurer, the state-owned PZU SA, will pay at least 160 million zlotys in damages caused by flooding while other insurers have no complete data on how much the disaster will cost them, officials said.
"According to data from Thursday, the amount of damages PZU will pay to our customers is 150-160 million zlotys but the amount will change," PZU's spokesman Marek Maszek told Reuters.
Insurer Polisa said damages it would have to pay for the floods would not be substantial.
"We have no damages estimates, but we have little insurance operations in the affected region," Polisa's deputy president Jerzy Rytlewski said.
Heavy floods which hit southern Poland six days ago have killed 23 people and put 3,400 square km under water.
PZU's Maszek said flood victims had filed 60,000 claims by Thursday. PZU will have to pay 30 million zlotys for damage to houses, farms and other buildings and 70,000 million for car damages.
Warta said it has no estimates for flood damages but that it had introduced simplified procedures to pay them.
"We will be able to talk about the scope of damages when water subsides," the firm's spokesman Zbigniew Augustynowicz said.
